ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is an independent Cl, with a negative charge labeled beside it; in the middle is a C=O fragment, with a double bond between carbon and oxygen, and a positive charge labeled beside oxygen; oxygen is also connected by a single bond to AlCl3 at the lower right, with a negative charge labeled near AlCl3. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the connected main fragment is carbon double-bonded to positively charged oxygen, and oxygen is then single-bonded to negatively charged aluminum trichloride, so it is written as C=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl. The independent chloride ion on the left is a separate component, written as [Cl-]. Different components are connected with a dot, so the complete SMILES is C=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl.[Cl-].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First inspect the chemical drawing and ignore all curved arrows. Identify the connected adduct as carbon double-bonded to positively charged oxygen, with that oxygen single-bonded to negatively charged aluminum trichloride. Encode this connected fragment as C=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl. Then identify the separate chloride ion shown at the left with a negative charge and encode it as [Cl-]. Join disconnected components with a dot to obtain the full SMILES.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧有一个独立的 Cl，旁边标有负电荷；中间是 C=O 片段，碳和氧之间为双键，氧旁标有正电荷；氧还通过单键连接到右下方的 AlCl3，AlCl3 附近标有负电荷。图中还有弯曲箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。
推理：忽略箭头后，连接的主片段是碳双键连到带正电的氧，氧再单键连到带负电的三氯铝，因此写作 C=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl。左侧独立的氯离子是单独组分，写作 [Cl-]。不同组分用点号连接，所以完整 SMILES 为 C=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl.[Cl-]。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions for charged atoms and connectivity: write C=O for the carbonyl double bond, bracket charged atoms as [O+] and [Al-], attach three chlorines to aluminum as [Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl, and separate disconnected species with a period; write free chloride as [Cl-].
